subject: Post-call: Cost qualification & preliminary ROI outline
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Rao <anika@novafin.com>, M. Gupta <mgupta@novafin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Cost qualification & preliminary ROI outline

Hi Anika / Mudit —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. I kept this short — please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- High per-interaction cost on billing alerts and reconciliation flows (spike during end-of-day runs).
- Unpredictable token usage driven by long system prompts + verbose user histories.
- Need predictable billing for Q4 launch; procurement requires a clear TCO for pilot.

Goals we agreed on:
- Prove 20–40% unit-cost reduction (tokens/$) within a 3–6 week pilot.
- Keep 95th percentile latency under 300ms for fast-path transactions.
- No production PII exfiltration; integrate with your KMS and audit logs.

Rough cost anchors (from today's call):
- Estimated baseline: ~120M tokens/month across alert+recon flows.
- Current third-party spend: ~USD 18k/month (approx).

Levers we'll pursue in the pilot:
1) Batching & microbatching for end-of-day reconciliation windows — expect biggest impact on throughput episodes.
2) Prefix and KV caching for repeated customer prompts — reduces repeated encoder cost.
3) Model/quantization profile: run medium-quality variant for high-volume paths, higher-quality for dispute triage.

Preliminary scenarios we'll deliver: conservative (pilot focuses on caching + small batching gains) and aggressive (full batching + routing + quantization). I'll circulate a short two-scenario ROI snapshot and the pilot scope sheet (attached).

Immediate asks from your side:
- Confirm target budget band for a paid pilot (ballpark is fine — we suggested $3k–$8k in the call).
- Share internal security contact for questionnaire (export controls & KMS scope) so we can start evidence handoff.
- Confirm decision stakeholders (procurement, platform, security) and their preferred cadence.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll send a short cost scenario doc + pilot scope by EOD tomorrow.
- Benedict (Ben) will draft a lightweight mutual action plan for approvals and timelines.
- Schedule a 30-min alignment with your security contact next week.

Attachments: pilot_scope_sheet.xlsx (pilot milestones + ops checklist) — redwood_token_econ_v1.pdf (two-scenario ROI).

Thanks again — talk soon.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful and matches our notes. A couple quick asks/questions before you send the scenarios: 

1) Can you show two explicit cost scenarios (conservative / aggressive) with monthly spend, expected savings, and an estimate of ops lift required from our infra team?
2) Security: who on your security/compliance team will own the SOC2/KMS conversation? We need a named contact so we can loop in our InfoSec.
3) SLA question: What latency SLOs do you commit to during a pilot vs production?

Budget: procurement asked me to confirm whether the pilot cap can be set at USD 6k — I don’t have final approval yet but that’s the band I can push.

If you can get the two scenarios + the pilot scope doc by EOD tomorrow that would be perfect. Also please include any assumptions (avg tokens per call; % of traffic eligible for batching).

Best,

Hi Anika / Mudit —

Thanks for the pointer, Vanessa. Attached are the two requested scenarios (redwood_token_econ_v1.pdf) and a short pilot scope (pilot_scope_sheet.xlsx). Key assumptions are also listed in the doc — pulled the most conservative estimates from our serving profile. Quick summary below.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline traffic: 120M tokens/month (mix of short alert prompts and long reconciliation prompts).
- Current spend: USD 18,000/month (as-discussed).
- % of traffic we can cache: 25% (conservative); up to 50% in aggressive.
- Batching opportunity: small during steady-state (10–15%) but large during reconciliation windows (up to 60% if we microbatch).

Scenario A — Conservative (pilot-focused) - Estimated net spend during pilot month: USD 14,400 - Expected savings vs baseline: ~20% (~USD 3,600/month) - Implementation lift: minimal infra changes (edge-cache + small routing rule), 1–2 weeks of engineering time

Scenario B — Aggressive (full-levers)
- Estimated net spend during target month: USD 9,900
- Expected savings vs baseline: ~45% (~USD 8,100/month)
- Implementation lift: moderate (batching pipeline + routing + KV cache tuning), 3–5 weeks of engineering effort

Notes on SLA during pilot:
- We aim to maintain 95th percentile latency <= 300ms on fast-paths for pilot traffic we route to optimized pools; we will tag non-critical traffic for high-throughput lanes with relaxed P95.

Security point of contact: Priya Natarajan (Security & Compliance, RedWood) will lead the questionnaire and KMS integration. I’ve included her contact in the Drive folder linked in the docs.

Next actions we suggest:
1) Confirm pilot cap (Anika: can you confirm USD 6k is acceptable as a pilot not-to-exceed?)
2) Sign off on the mutual action plan in the pilot_scope_sheet (we can circulate a doc link for e-signature).
3) Align on an InfoSec call (Priya + your security lead) — suggested window next Tue/Wed.

I’ll follow up with a short spreadsheet modeling month-0 (ramp) vs steady-state for the two scenarios if that helps procurement.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
